stories.title: Australian MP Helen Haines discharged after losing both legs in alleged car attack
stories.summary: Independent MP Helen Haines, who lost both legs after a white Toyota LandCruiser was driven into her outside her Wangaratta electorate office on 19 October, has been released from hospital. Police have charged 43‑year‑old Brendan Nugent with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and the federal offence of causing harm to a public official, and he has not yet entered a plea.
stories.why: The case highlights the legal response to violent attacks on elected officials.

stories.title: Paris police ban protests near 10 schools and five universities for five days
stories.summary: Paris police have issued a five‑day ban on unauthorised gatherings within 100 metres of ten secondary schools and five universities, effective 16–20 November. The order was announced by police chief Patrice Faure, who said it was needed because of numerous disruptions, blockades and persistent violence around the sites. The protests, which began in September over secondary‑school conditions, have spread to universities, workers and the yellow‑vest movement.
stories.why: The ban restricts demonstrations near educational institutions, aiming to reduce disruptions and violence that have affected schools and universities.

stories.title: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi raises $24 million seed round for AI image sensors
stories.summary: Bharat Semi, an Indian semiconductor startup of almost five years, announced a $24 million seed funding round to develop AI‑enabled programmable image sensors. The company says it has secured design wins with U.S. defense firm General Atomics and India’s Kaynes Semicon, and it aims to begin commercial production of its single‑chip sensor that combines capture, processing and AI in 2027. Co‑founder Vrinda Kapoor claims the chip could cut system costs by at least 70 % versus conventional multi‑chip solutions.
stories.why: The capital will speed development of low‑cost, AI‑ready vision chips that could help Indian and global firms diversify semiconductor supply chains.

stories.title: Prince Harry makes surprise visit to Lviv to meet injured Ukrainian veterans
stories.summary: Prince Harry made a surprise two‑day visit to Lviv, Ukraine, where he met injured Ukrainian service members and competitors from his Invictus Games. He was applauded by veterans, toured projects that provide treatment and rehabilitation, and said, “You’re going to win the war.” A press blackout was maintained for security while the country faced ongoing Russian missile attacks.
stories.why: This matters because it could expand treatment options or demonstrate a clinically meaningful new medical technology.
